Content: The lionfish is a venomous fish found primarily in the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. In the `text(1990s)`, lionfish were accidentally released into the Atlantic Ocean, where they found abundant resources and favorable environmental conditions. Which of the following scenarios is most likely to result in the lionfish having a major impact on the communities into which they were introduced?

A.Choice: With no natural predators, the lionfish population will become very large.

B.Choice: Some native species of invertebrates will develop a resistance to lionfish venom.

C.Choice: Random mating will allow the lionfish population to reach Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

D.Choice: A virus that specifically infects lionfish will become more prevalent.

Content: Cell communication is critical for the function of both unicellular and multicellular eukaryotes. Which of the following is likely true of cell signaling?

A.Choice: Cell signaling uses the highest molecular weight molecules found in living cells.

B.Choice: Cell signaling has largely been replaced by other cell functions in higher mammals.

C.Choice: Similar cell signaling pathways in diverse eukaryotes are evidence of conserved evolutionary processes.

D.Choice: Cell signaling functions mainly during early developmental stages.

Content: A colony of termites was exposed to an atmosphere of `100` `text(percent)` oxygen for `text(three days)`. The insects were not immediately harmed by the treatment, but the protozoa that lived in the termites' guts were eliminated. The treated termites continued to behave normally and to eat wood, but they began to starve after a short time.

When the treated termites were instead fed wood contaminated with the feces of untreated termites, the treated termites regained the ability to digest wood and no longer starved. The best analysis of the results of the experiment is that

A.Choice: infection with protozoa causes the termites to switch to fermentation

B.Choice: cooperative interactions between the termites and the protozoa allow termites to extract energy from wood to survive

C.Choice: the termite immune system eliminates protozoa from the gut

D.Choice: termites digest protozoa as their main source of energy

Content: Ethylene is an organic compound produced by ripening fruits. In a controlled experiment, researchers found that ethylene gas stimulated the ripening process in newly harvested fruits. Which of the following describes the most likely connection between natural ethylene production and fruit ripening?

A.Choice: As a result of metabolic inactivity, newly harvested fruits are unable to absorb ethylene gas from the atmosphere.

B.Choice: Ethylene gas is a chemical signal through which ripening fruits trigger the ripening process in other fruits.

C.Choice: Because of normal phenotypic variation, only some of the fruits in a given generation are expected to produce ethylene gas.

D.Choice: The rate of ethylene gas production by ripening fruits is an indicator of the relative age of an ecosystem.

Content: Water in a pond contaminated with the weed killer atrazine is suspected of inhibiting metamorphosis in northern leopard frogs. A team of scientists collected fertilized northern leopard frog eggs from a different pond that is not contaminated. Which of the following is the best experimental design to determine whether atrazine is responsible for inhibiting metamorphosis in northern leopard frogs?

A.Choice: Place `text(half)` of the fertilized eggs in a pool of water with the same concentration of atrazine as the contaminated pond and place the other `text(half)` of the fertilized eggs in a pool of water that has no atrazine. Monitor the development of the embryos through metamorphosis into adulthood.

B.Choice: Place all of the fertilized eggs in a pool of pond water with the same concentration of atrazine as the contaminated pond and compare the number of frogs that reach metamorphosis to those that reach adulthood in the contaminated pond.

C.Choice: Allow all fertilized eggs to develop into adults. Expose `text(one-third)` of the frogs to `text(one-half)` of the concentration of atrazine in the contaminated pond and expose another `text(one-third)` of the frogs to the same concentration of atrazine as the contaminated pond. Leave the last `text(one-third)` of the frogs in water with no atrazine and note any adverse changes in the physical condition of the atrazine-treated frogs in `text(three months)`.

D.Choice: Divide the fertilized eggs into `text(three)` groups and expose `text(each group)` to a different concentration of atrazine. Release the eggs back into the contaminated pond and check for metamorphosis after `text(three months)`.

Content: Which of the following best explains how biological communities near deep-sea hydrothermal vents can exist in a habitat lacking sunlight?

A.Choice: Environmental conditions on some distant planets resemble those experienced by organisms living near hydrothermal vents.

B.Choice: Heterotrophs metabolize carbon-containing compounds produced by the photosynthetic organisms that live on the seafloor.

C.Choice: Some organisms rely on energy captured from inorganic compounds to drive basic biological processes.

D.Choice: Some organisms that can tolerate high temperatures are `text(single)` celled, whereas others are multicellular.

Content: Based on an analysis of the food web, an observation that deep-sea bacteria consume molecular hydrogen (`text(H)_2`) is most relevant to resolving which of the following apparent contradictions?

A.Choice: Water gushing from deep-sea hydrothermal vents can be as hot as `400°text(C)`, which is a lethal temperature for most organisms.

B.Choice: Some deep-sea organisms appear to be primary consumers, but no plants live near the hydrothermal vents.

C.Choice: Zoarcid fish are thought to be aggressive predators, but they are frequently described as being lazy swimmers.

D.Choice: Some tissues of tubeworms contain hemoglobin, which is an oxygen-carrying molecule, but there is little free oxygen at this depth.

Content: Researchers are investigating the evolutionary relationships among organisms found near deep-sea hydrothermal vents and similar organisms found closer to the ocean surface. Which of the following scientific questions is most relevant to the investigation?

A.Choice: What are the nucleotide sequences of ribosomal `text(RNA)` genes that are found in the genomes of the different species?

B.Choice: What large-scale geological events have occurred recently in the Mid-Atlantic Ocean?

C.Choice: Does water temperature at different ocean depths affect the relative levels of dissolved oxygen?

D.Choice: Do species found near deep-sea hydrothermal vents all have the same haploid number of chromosomes?

Content: On the basis of the food web, which of the following members of a deep-sea biological community is most likely to also have a symbiotic relationship with chemosynthetic organisms?

A.Choice: Octopuses

B.Choice: Blind crabs

C.Choice: Zoarcid fish

D.Choice: Shrimp

Content: To refine their model of deep-sea biological communities, the researchers investigated areas of the seafloor that are distant from any active hydrothermal vents. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the observation that some octopus species are only found near active hydrothermal vents?

A.Choice: Octopuses depend indirectly on inorganic compounds in the seawater surrounding hydrothermal vents.

B.Choice: Organisms capable of moving across the seafloor are more difficult to observe than are organisms that are rooted in place.

C.Choice: Genetic bottleneck events in isolated areas of the deep ocean adversely affect some octopus populations but not others.

D.Choice: Biomass in a typical marine food web is expected to be greater in higher trophic levels than in lower trophic levels.

Content: On a large volcanic island, researchers are studying a population of `text(annual)` herbaceous plants. Which of the following observations best supports the prediction that speciation will occur within the existing plant population?

A.Choice: Individuals of the species sometimes reproduce asexually by producing runners.

B.Choice: Lava has separated the population into `text(two)` areas: an upland forest and a lowland marsh.

C.Choice: Multiple groups of birds depend on the fruit produced by the plants as a source of food.

D.Choice: The plants produce more seeds during warm summers than they do during cool summers.

Content: Individuals with an inherited autosomal recessive disorder called primary ciliary dyskinesia (`text(PCD)`) often have severe respiratory problems due to defective cilia. Males with `text(PCD)` are often sterile because they produce sperm with defective flagella. Which of the following most likely explains the effect of the recessive allele?

A.Choice: The mitochondria are defective and do not produce sufficient protein to synthesize microtubules in the cilia and flagella.

B.Choice: The plasma membrane of the alveoli is not permeable to carbon dioxide during respiration because it is too hydrophobic.

C.Choice: The Golgi bodies secrete an enzyme that destroys the proteins in the flagella and cilia.

D.Choice: The cells do not produce functional motor proteins in flagella and cilia.

Content: The salinity of a small inland lake has recently started to increase. Researchers are planning to study the lake over several `text(decades)` to investigate how freshwater organisms survive significant changes in their natural habitat. Which of the following physiological mechanisms will the researchers most likely observe among the surviving organisms in the lake?

A.Choice: Prokaryotic organisms will use various mechanisms to counteract swelling of cells as a result of increased water uptake.

B.Choice: `text(Single-celled)` organisms will use various mechanisms to counteract the increased flow of water from cells to the environment.

C.Choice: Eukaryotic organisms will use various mechanisms to counteract the diffusion of positively charged ions across the cell membrane.

D.Choice: Multicellular organisms will use various mechanisms to counteract the loss of cell adhesion as a result of calcium deficiencies.

Content: Which of the following best explains the differences in the armor of the Lake Washington stickleback population summarized in Figure `1`?

A.Choice: Analysis of somatic cells using chromosomal staining and light microscopy indicates that stickleback fish have a diploid number of `42`.

B.Choice: Stickleback males from natural freshwater populations are typically more aggressive when competing for mates than are stickleback males from laboratory-bred populations.

C.Choice: Fish exhibiting the low-plated phenotype were selected against in the Lake Washington stickleback population over the last `50` `text(years)`.

D.Choice: Migration of individuals from other freshwater environments to Lake Washington led to gene flow between populations that were once geographically isolated.

Content: A completely-plated stickleback from a marine population was mated to a low-plated stickleback from a freshwater population. The resulting `text(F)_1` hybrids all displayed a completely plated phenotype. When the `text(F)_1` hybrids were allowed to interbreed, the resulting `text(F)_2` generation included completely plated offspring and low-plated offspring in an approximate `3:1` ratio. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by the results of the breeding experiments?

A.Choice: Phenotypic variation in the `text(F)_2` generation suggests that armor morphology is controlled by many alleles of a `text(single)` gene.

B.Choice: The completely-plated phenotype is controlled by a dominant allele of a `text(single)` gene.

C.Choice: Armor loss is an acquired characteristic that is affected by `text(one)` or more environmental factors.

D.Choice: Patterns of armor plating in stickleback populations are regulated by sex-specific signals.

Content: Prior to `text(1960)`, Lake Washington was highly polluted and underwater visibility was limited to `text(one)` or `text(two meters)`. In the `text(late 1960s)`, a large cleanup effort reduced pollution, resulting in visibility that increased to `text(six)` to `text(seven meters)` by `text(1976)`. Which of the following best explains how the change in underwater visibility affected armor plating in Lake Washington sticklebacks between `text(1957)` and `text(1976)`?

A.Choice: Higher visibility allowed sticklebacks to increase their food consumption to make armor production easier.

B.Choice: Higher visibility made the sticklebacks more susceptible to large-toothed predators in the lakes, giving complete armor a selective advantage.

C.Choice: Clearer water allowed sunlight to penetrate to deeper depths, so the sticklebacks had to increase the amount of armor to protect themselves from the resulting increase in water temperature.

D.Choice: Clearer water contained fewer of the molecular building blocks needed for armor production, so sticklebacks showed a reduction in the amount of armor.

Content: Evolution of a new trait typically takes many generations. Yet a dramatic shift in the extent of armor plating in the Lake Washington stickleback population occurred in the `50` `text(years)` following the cleanup of the lake. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of the rapid evolution of the armor phenotype in the Lake Washington sticklebacks?

A.Choice: Pollutants in Lake Washington forced the sticklebacks to increase their mutation rate.

B.Choice: The rapid change in the Lake Washington ecosystem required individual sticklebacks to evolve complete armor quickly.

C.Choice: The increase in visibility in Lake Washington allowed sticklebacks to visually select mates with low armor.

D.Choice: New selective pressures favored individuals with the plated phenotype, causing the plated allele frequency in the population to quickly increase.

Content: The phylogenetic trees in Figures `2` and `3` depict `text(two)` different phylogenies of the same populations of sticklebacks. Which of the following questions will best help determine which tree represents the most accurate phylogeny?

A.Choice: Is the `text(EDA)` gene as representative of the differences between the populations as the `25` random genes that were examined for Figure `3`?

B.Choice: Are the low-plated populations found only in freshwater and the high-plated populations found only in saltwater environments?

C.Choice: Is the common ancestor of the organisms represented in Figure `2` different from the common ancestor of the organisms represented in Figure `3`?

D.Choice: Is the expression level of the `text(EDA)` gene analyzed in Figure `2` significantly greater than the expression levels of the `25` genes analyzed in Figure `3`?

Content: A researcher examining a root tip observes a plant cell with condensed sister chromatids, kinetochores with attached microtubules, and individual chromosomes that are aligned at the equatorial plate of the cell. Which of the following best describes what the next process will be in the cell?

A.Choice: Homologous chromosomes (each with `text(two)` sister chromatids) will move toward opposite poles of the cell.

B.Choice: Paired chromatids will separate, and the new daughter chromosomes will move toward opposite poles of the cell.

C.Choice: The nuclear envelope will break down, and the spindle will begin to form.

D.Choice: The chromatin will decondense, and the daughter cell will enter interphase.

Chytridiomycosis is a potentially lethal fungal infection that adversely affects some frog populations. The incidence and severity of the fungal infection can vary over time. Which of the following statements best describes the changes in the frog population that are depicted in the model above?

Content: The pesticide `text(DDT)` was widely used in the `text(1940s)` as a method of insect control. In the late `text(1950s)` the `text(first)` `text(DDT-resistant)` mosquitoes were discovered, and eventually `text(DDT-resistant)` mosquitoes were found globally. When `text(DDT)` is used now, the development of `text(DDT)` resistance in mosquito populations occurs in months rather than years.
Which of the following best explains the observations concerning `text(DDT)` resistance in mosquitoes?

A.Choice: Competition for limited resources causes mosquitoes to migrate to geographical areas that have richer supplies of `text(DDT)`.

B.Choice: The proportion of `text(DDT-resistant)` mosquitoes in a population remains constant due to the metabolic costs of `text(DDT)` utilization.

C.Choice: Natural selection favors `text(DDT-resistant)` mosquitoes that are already present in a population when `text(DDT)` exposure occurs.

D.Choice: `text(DDT)` is a chemical signal that delays normal reproductive cycles in many mosquito populations.

Content: `text(Two)` nutrient solutions are maintained at the same `text(pH)`. Actively respiring mitochondria are isolated and placed into each of the `text(two)` solutions. Oxygen gas is bubbled into `text(one)` solution. The other solution is depleted of available oxygen. Which of the following best explains why `text(ATP)` production is greater in the tube with oxygen than in the tube without oxygen?

A.Choice: The rate of proton pumping across the inner mitochondrial membrane is lower in the sample without oxygen.

B.Choice: Electron transport is reduced in the absence of a plasma membrane.

C.Choice: In the absence of oxygen, oxidative phosphorylation produces more `text(ATP)` than does fermentation.

D.Choice: In the presence of oxygen, glycolysis produces more `text(ATP)` than in the absence of oxygen.

However, many testcross offspring have the same phenotype as one of the `text(two)` plants in the parental cross, but relatively few testcross offspring have the same phenotype as the `text(F)_1` offspring. Which of the following best explains the observation?

Content: When a stimulus is applied to a receptor in the skin, an action potential is propagated along a neuron to the brain, where another signal is sent back to the muscle for a response.

B.Choice: The action potential travels through the synapse to the next connecting dendrite.

C.Choice: The action potential jumps the synapse to the next connecting dendrite.

D.Choice: The action potential causes a release of neurotransmitters that travel across the synapse.

Content: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (`text(MRSA)`) can be a serious threat to human health. There is evidence that S. aureus infections are common in hospitals and that `text(MRSA)` have become resistant to other antibiotics besides methicillin. This suggests that the rapid evolution of resistance in the bacteria poses a serious public-health challenge. Which of the following best explains the ability of `text(MRSA)` to evade existing drug therapies?

A.Choice: `text(MRSA)` have very long generation times and very large population sizes.

B.Choice: `text(MRSA)` develop new alleles by intentionally introducing specific mutations that will give them a selective advantage over other bacteria.

C.Choice: `text(MRSA)` metabolize many drugs in their lysosomes and therefore evolve resistance at a high rate.

D.Choice: `text(MRSA)` exchange genetic material with other antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which can spread resistance in the S. aureus population.

Content: Which of the following best describes an advantage that eukaryote organisms have over prokaryote organisms?

A.Choice: Prokaryotes lack a cell membrane and therefore are unable to control what enters or exits the cell.

B.Choice: Eukaryotes have a nuclear envelope separating their `text(DNA)` from the rest of the cell, which increases the likelihood of advantageous mutations.

C.Choice: Eukaryotes have mitochondria and chloroplasts that contain their own genome, which allows the cells to reproduce more rapidly.

D.Choice: Eukaryotes have organelles that allow for compartmentalization of cellular processes, which increases the efficiency of those processes.
